When one of those drivers causes an accident, the injured victim is not dealing with an individual. They are dealing with a corporation backed by experienced adjusters and defense attorneys whose job is to limit the company’s payments.
Our
Denver UPS truck accident lawyers

We move quickly to secure and analyze that material before it is altered or lost, and we use it to build claims that reflect the full scope of our clients’ suffering.

How Can a Denver UPS Truck Accident Lawyer Help Me?

Collisions involving commercial delivery vehicles are more legally complex than standard car accident claims. Multiple parties may share liability, federal and state regulations apply simultaneously, and the carrier’s insurer deploys experienced professionals to manage your claim from day one. Having a
Denver UPS truck accident lawyer
on your side from the start makes a concrete difference across every stage of your case:
Preserving
Critical Evidence
Delivery records, GPS tracking data, dashcam footage, and electronic logging device data are time-sensitive. We move immediately to secure and analyze this material before it disappears.
Identifying All Liable Parties
Depending on the facts, responsibility may extend beyond the driver to UPS as the employer, a third-party maintenance provider, or a cargo loading company.
Calculating Full Damages
We account for current and future medical costs, lost income, reduced earning capacity, pain and suffering, and other compensable losses under Colorado law.
Handling All Insurer Communications:

Taking the Case to Trial:
When insurers refuse to offer fair compensation, we are prepared to litigate. Our trial record shows we follow through.
Understanding what your attorney can do for you is one part of the picture. Knowing what caused the crash in the first place is where building a strong claim begins.
Common Causes of UPS Truck Accidents in Denver

Denver’s combination of dense urban traffic, major interstate freight corridors, and unpredictable seasonal weather creates conditions that amplify the risks already present in high-volume delivery operations. UPS drivers operating under demanding daily delivery quotas face consistent pressure that compounds each of these factors, and when something goes wrong on a Denver street or highway, the consequences for other drivers can be severe.
The most common contributing factors in Denver UPS truck accidents include:
Driver Fatigue:
Demanding delivery schedules frequently push drivers past safe working limits. The
National Safety Council
identifies fatigue as one of the most underreported hazards in commercial driving.
Distracted Driving
Constant GPS rerouting, handheld device use, and route-checking pull a driver’s attention away from the road at critical moments.
Improper Cargo Loading:
Overloaded or unevenly distributed packages shift during transit, affecting vehicle handling and braking response.
Poor Vehicle Maintenance:
Brake failures, tire blowouts, and steering defects can lead to catastrophic outcomes when maintenance schedules are skipped or delayed.
Adverse Weather Conditions:
Denver winters bring ice, snow, and reduced visibility that demand adjusted speeds and greater stopping distances, conditions that delivery pressure often overrides.
Aggressive Driving on I-25 and I-70:
Tight delivery schedules push drivers to navigate Denver’s busiest corridors at unsafe speeds or with insufficient following distances.
Understanding what caused the crash is the foundation of every strong claim, and Colorado law determines what happens next.
Who Can Be Held Liable After a UPS Truck Accident?

More than one party can be held responsible after a UPS truck accident, and identifying all of them is essential to maximizing your recovery. Depending on the circumstances, liability may extend to the following:
UPS as the Employer:
UPS drivers are W-2 employees, which means the company is directly responsible for their actions on the job.
The UPS Driver:
Personal liability applies when the driver was fatigued, distracted, speeding, or otherwise negligent.
A Maintenance Provider:
If a mechanical failure contributed to the crash and a third party serviced the vehicle, they may share responsibility.
Another Driver:
In multi-vehicle crashes, a third driver’s negligence may have contributed.
Our team investigates all of these angles from the start, so nothing is overlooked.
Colorado’s Laws for UPS Truck Accident Claims
Two Colorado statutes directly shape your claim after a UPS truck accident in Denver.
The first is the comparative fault rule. Under
Colorado Revised Statutes § 13-21-111
, you can still recover compensation even if you were partially at fault, as long as your share stays below 50 percent:
If you are found 20 percent at fault, you recover 80 percent of your damages
At 50 percent or more, you recover nothing
UPS’s insurer will almost always try to raise that percentage, making attorney review of any fault determination essential
The second is the filing deadline. Under
Colorado Revised Statutes § 13-80-101

, you have three years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury claim, though that window closes faster than most people expect. Evidence fades, witnesses become harder to locate, and UPS begins building its defense from day one.
Beyond state law, federal regulations add another layer of accountability. UPS drivers and vehicles must comply with
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration standards
covering:
Hours-of-service limits for commercial drivers
Regular vehicle inspection and maintenance requirements
Cargo securement protocols

Violations of those standards can establish negligence directly and significantly strengthen your claim. What you do in the hours and days after the crash determines how effectively these protections can work for you.
What Steps Should I Take Immediately After a UPS Truck Accident in Denver?

The decisions made in the hours following a collision can have a lasting effect on the strength of a claim. UPS carries significant insurance coverage and deploys corporate response resources quickly. Taking the right steps from the start gives you the best chance at a full recovery:
Seek Medical Attention Right Away:

Your health comes first, and a medical evaluation creates an official record linking your injuries to the crash. Do not wait, even if you feel fine at the scene. Many truck accident injuries surface hours or days after the accident.
Call Law Enforcement:
A police report documents what happened, who was involved, and whether the UPS driver received any citations. That report becomes an important piece of evidence in your claim.
Document the Scene:
Take photos of everything before vehicles are moved: the damage, road conditions, skid marks, and any UPS vehicle markings or visible cargo. The more detail, the better.
Get Witness Information:
If anyone saw the crash, ask for their name and phone number. An independent account of what happened can carry significant weight when liability is disputed.
Do Not Give a Recorded Statement:
UPS’s insurance team may contact you quickly and ask for your version of events. Politely decline until you have spoken with an attorney. What you say can be used to reduce or deny your claim.
Contact a Denver UPS Truck Accident Lawyer:
Early legal involvement means evidence is preserved, deadlines are tracked, and you have someone in your corner before the other side gets too far ahead.
Taking these steps protects your claim from the start and prepares you for what comes next, including understanding the full range of injuries these collisions can cause.
Injuries Common in Delivery Truck Collisions

A fully loaded UPS delivery truck can weigh up to 26,000 pounds, while the average passenger vehicle weighs around 4,000. On Denver streets and highways, that gap in size and force is why collisions with delivery trucks so often result in severe, long-lasting, or permanent injuries. Many of these injuries are not immediately apparent at the scene, which makes prompt medical evaluation not just advisable but critical.
Some of the most common injuries include:
Traumatic brain injuries
, including concussions and more severe cognitive impairments
Spinal cord injuries
resulting in partial or full paralysis
Broken bones and fractures requiring surgery or prolonged rehabilitation
Internal organ damage from blunt-force impact
Soft tissue injuries to the neck, back, and shoulders
Lacerations and scarring from glass, metal, or road contact
Emotional and psychological trauma, including post-traumatic stress
The severity of these injuries directly affects the value of a claim. Compensation available under Colorado law includes economic and non-economic damages, and
Dormer Harpring
works to ensure every loss is thoroughly documented from the start. The stronger the foundation, the better positioned your claim will be for recovery.
Compensation You May Be Entitled to After a UPS Truck Accident

When another party’s negligence causes a collision, Colorado law allows injured victims to pursue compensation that reflects the full impact of what they have been through, not just the immediate costs. A UPS truck accident can disrupt every aspect of your life, from your ability to work to your long-term physical and emotional well-being, and the compensation available to you should account for all of it.
Economic damages cover the measurable financial losses tied directly to the crash:
Medical expenses, including emergency care, surgery, hospitalization, and follow-up treatment
Future medical costs for ongoing rehabilitation, therapy, or long-term care needs
Lost wages from time away from work during recovery
Reduced earning capacity if your injuries affect your ability to work long-term
Property damage for vehicle repairs or replacement
Non-economic damages reflect the personal impact the crash has had on your life:
Physical pain and suffering
Emotional distress and anxiety
Loss of enjoyment of life
Permanent scarring or disfigurement
Loss of companionship or consortium for affected family members

In cases where UPS or its driver acted with particular recklessness or disregard for safety, Colorado law may also allow for punitive damages on top of compensatory losses. These are not awarded in every case, but when the conduct that caused the crash was especially egregious, they can significantly increase the total recovery.

The full value of a claim is rarely obvious at the outset. Injuries evolve, future care needs become clearer over time, and the non-economic impact of a serious crash can take months to fully understand. Getting an accurate picture of what your case is worth is one of the most important things an attorney can do for you early in the process.

faqs.question: What are my legal rights after an accident involving a UPS vehicle?

children.text: You have the right to pursue compensation for medical costs, lost income, and pain and suffering directly from UPS.

faqs.question: How do Colorado laws impact my UPS truck accident claim?

children.text: Colorado’s comparative fault rule reduces your recovery by your fault percentage; a three-year filing deadline also applies.
